why: The statement asks only whether infinitely many Fibonacci primes exist. Proven and probable new Fibonacci primes are finite instances. Grantham-Granville is a heuristic and the formalisation only states the problem, so both are none. The Lucas-sequence, bounded-gap, Polignac-type, perfect-number and index-pattern papers answer different questions, so they are variants. Park's paper is human-led, and GPT-6 Astra found the example in it, so it is assisted, but its question is a variant. The SOVEREIGN deposit does not say the system is an AI and names no model, so its role is none; the scope discards it either way. The ResearchGate claim would be whole, but it has no readable content and no date, it got no uptake, and later experts still call the problem open, so I judge it not_credible. Year-only 2025 dates are certainly after 26 January 2024, but I give the Integers and formal-conjectures events null because the record cannot place their precise dates. Their scope discards them anyway.
doubts: The year-only 2025 events are certainly after the snapshot. They are null here only out of caution, and since both are discarded this changes nothing. The ResearchGate claim's date and author are unestablished. Its URL id suggests a pre-2024 posting, but that is not shown in the record. Park's AI quote came through a summarising fetch.
